newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hopes China follows democracy path after Deng.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hopes China follows democracy path after Deng.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign ministry said on Thursday it hoped rival Beijing would follow a path towards democracy and recognise Taipei as an "equal political entity" following the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
Deng died on Wednesday night at the age of 92.

"We hope that the Chinese Communist leadership will continue to implement the ongoing economic reform programmes and, in conformity with the world trend of democracy, strive to enhance the social stability and welfare of the people on the mainland," the ministry said in a statement.
It added that Beijing should respect Taipei's sovereignty.

"It is our earnest hope that the authorities on the mainland will take a more rational and pragmatic attitude and face up to the reality that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, being two equal political entities, are under separate jurisdiction," the ministry said.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war ended in 1949. China considers Taiwan a renegade province to be brought eventually under Beijing's rule, by force if necessary.
Taiwan maintains it is a legitimate government and would agree to reunite with the mainland only if Beijing adopts democratic reforms.
The foreign ministry said Taipei was "well prepared for contingencies" regarding political developments on the mainland in the wake of Deng's passing. It did not elaborate.
